plan.chapter_thesis: Metasurface holography rests on three distinct phase control mechanisms—geometric (Pancharatnam-Berry) phase, propagation (resonant) phase, and hybrid approaches—each imposing fundamentally different trade-offs among efficiency, bandwidth, polarization sensitivity, and design flexibility that constrain all downstream applications.
plan.reader_takeaway: The choice of phase control mechanism (geometric vs. propagation vs. hybrid) dictates the fundamental limits of a holographic device's efficiency, color fidelity, and polarization handling, necessitating specific inverse design strategies to navigate these physical constraints.

argument_sequence.purpose: Establish the physical foundation of wavefront engineering and the role of subwavelength structures in manipulating light properties.
Define geometric phase (Pancharatnam-Berry) as a mechanism relying on orientation rotation, highlighting its polarization dependence.
Define propagation phase via resonant effects and optical path length, introducing bound states and dispersion challenges.
Introduce hybrid approaches that combine metallic and dielectric elements to balance field confinement and loss.
Characterize the intrinsic trade-offs (efficiency, bandwidth, polarization) inherent to each mechanism.
Explain the transition from heuristic design to automated inverse design required to navigate these complex parameter spaces.
Detail deep learning and data-driven methods as solutions for mapping non-linear geometry-response relationships.
Describe gradient-based and adjoint optimization techniques for high-fidelity wavefront reconstruction.
Address the ill-posed nature of inverse design and the need for representation learning to handle non-uniqueness.
Synthesize how these physical mechanisms and design tools collectively enable multi-channel and multifunctional holography.

terminology_rows.note: Phase shift induced by spatial rotation of anisotropic nanostructures; inherently polarization-dependent.
Phase accumulation derived from optical path length variations or resonant delays within the meta-atom.
Resonant states with theoretically infinite quality factors used to enhance field confinement and phase modulation.
Computational framework mapping desired electromagnetic responses to optimal nanostructure geometries.
Gradient-based method using affine transformations to efficiently explore high-dimensional design spaces.

explanation_block_rows.title: Foundations of Wavefront Engineering
explanation_block_rows.goal: Establish metasurfaces as the platform for subwavelength light control governed by Maxwell's equations.

explanation_block_rows.title: Mechanism I: Geometric Phase Control
explanation_block_rows.goal: Define Pancharatnam-Berry phase, explain its origin in coordinate rotation, and note its polarization selectivity.

explanation_block_rows.title: Mechanism II: Propagation and Resonant Phase
explanation_block_rows.goal: Explain phase accumulation via optical path length and resonances (BICs/Fano), highlighting chromatic dispersion limits.

explanation_block_rows.title: Mechanism III: Hybrid and Dielectric Approaches
explanation_block_rows.goal: Present hybrid metal-dielectric and high-index dielectric strategies as means to balance efficiency and confinement.

explanation_block_rows.title: Intrinsic Trade-offs and Degrees of Freedom
explanation_block_rows.goal: Synthesize how meta-atom properties dictate available degrees of freedom and introduce non-uniqueness challenges.

explanation_block_rows.title: The Shift to Automated Inverse Design
explanation_block_rows.goal: Contrast traditional heuristic design with modern automated frameworks necessitated by complex phase mechanisms.

explanation_block_rows.title: Deep Learning for Non-Linear Mapping
explanation_block_rows.goal: Detail how neural networks learn non-linear input-output relationships to streamline bianisotropic and multifunctional design.

explanation_block_rows.title: Gradient-Based and Adjoint Optimization
explanation_block_rows.goal: Explain topology optimization and adjoint methods for achieving feasible fabrication results from continuous profiles.

explanation_block_rows.title: Resolving Ill-Posed Inverse Problems
explanation_block_rows.goal: Address the non-uniqueness of inverse scattering and the role of representation learning in stabilizing solutions.

explanation_block_rows.title: Enabling Multi-Channel Holography
explanation_block_rows.goal: Demonstrate how combined mechanisms and advanced algorithms enable spin, wavelength, and spatial multiplexing.
